extracted.intended_audience: practitioners and parties in PTAB trials (petitioners, patent owners/respondents, and their counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on procedure, motions, timing, evidence, claim amendments, and protective order practices for PTAB trials (IPR, PGR, CBM, and derivation proceedings). Intended to direct parties and counsel in preparing and litigating these administrative trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation petition requirements (35 U.S.C. 135(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to institute a derivation proceeding must state with particularity the basis for finding that a named inventor in the earlier application derived the claimed invention from an inventor named in the petitioner’s application, and without authorization filed the earlier application; must be filed within one year of the first publication by the earlier applicant of a claim to the same or substantially the same invention; must be made under oath; and must be supported by substantial evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: In deciding whether to institute a review, the Board will consider whether the party has satisfied the relevant statutory institution standard and may take into account whether the same or substantially the same prior art or arguments were previously presented to the Office under 35 U.S.C. 325(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may decline institution where prior presentation under 325(d) applies; the petition must demonstrate the statutory thresholds to institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and feasibility as institution factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may consider whether the review can be completed timely and may decline to institute a proceeding it determines it cannot complete in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example refusal: petition that seeks review of several hundred claims based on a thousand references where resolving patentability would require compelled testimony of dozens of foreign non-party witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of authorization when instituting
rubrics_metrics.description: When instituting a trial, the Board will streamline issues by authorizing the trial only on the challenged claims for which threshold standards are met and will identify, on a claim-by-claim basis, the grounds on which the trial will proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any claim or issue not included in the authorization is not part of the trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of a decision not to institute
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no trial is instituted, the Board will provide a decision which generally contains a short statement as to why the standards were not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board’s determination whether to institute a trial is final and nonappealable (citations to statutes provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling Order requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Scheduling Order will be provided concurrent with the decision to institute and will set due dates that account for complexity but ensure the trial is completed within one year of institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may request changes at the initial conference call and may stipulate different dates for Due Dates 1–5 (but not beyond Due Date 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial conference call procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board expects to initiate a conference call about one month after institution to discuss the Scheduling Order and anticipated motions; parties generally must provide a list of proposed motions no later than two business days prior to the call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete motions list helps adjust schedules, determine necessary/sufficient motions, and reveal possible dispositive issues; additional motions may require prior authorization and may not change set times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response (post-institution)
rubrics_metrics.description: For IPR, PGR, and CBM the patent owner may respond once a trial is instituted; for derivation the alleged deriving applicant/patent owner may respond once instituted. The patent owner response is filed as an opposition and is subject to page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response should identify involved claims believed patentable, state the basis for that belief, include affidavits or factual evidence and explain relevance, and may include a claim chart. If no response is filed the owner must arrange a conference call regarding possible request for adverse judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to amend — general (IPR/PGR/CBM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners may file motions to amend the claims subject to rules in §§ 42.121/42.221. The first motion to amend does not require prior authorization but the patent owner must confer with the Board before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference with the judge may provide guidance including impacts on schedule and whether additional discovery is appropriate; filing a motion to amend may prompt schedule adjustments and discovery authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional motions to amend authorization criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Any additional motions to amend after the first require Board authorization; authorization is typically granted if a joint request materially advances settlement or on a showing of good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will consider factors such as whether a petitioner submitted supplemental information about patentability after the time for filing a motion to amend, time remaining for trial, degree to which additional evidence impacts patentability, and whether the evidence was known to the patent owner earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend due date
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to amend must be filed no later than the time period for filing a patent owner response, unless a different due date is provided in a Board order; the Office envisions most motions to amend will be due about three months after institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a motion to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to amend must comply with content requirements in §§ 42.121(b) / 42.221(b): include a claim listing, show requested changes clearly, and describe how the original disclosure and any relied-on prior application support each claim added or amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent owner may not enlarge claim scope or add new matter; replacement claims should be identified as proposed substitute claims with all changes clearly discussed; must set forth support in original disclosure and any application for which benefit of filing date is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will interpret claims using the broadest reasonable construction consistent with statute and AIA legislative history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners may demonstrate that the amended claim's scope is substantially identical to the original patent claim as a district court would have interpreted it and request a determination under 35 U.S.C. 252 that they are substantially identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in derivation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to amend claims by parties in derivation proceedings will be authorized upon a showing of good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of good cause include materially advancing settlement or seeking to cancel claims. A request to cancel all disputed claims will be treated as a request for adverse judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: General practice tips on amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to amend should be filed by the due dates; authorization to file later in the proceeding requires demonstration of good cause; late-filed motions may impair the petitioner's ability to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions to cancel claims will generally be permitted even late, as will motions to correct simple and obvious typographical errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements for proposed amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to amend must be accompanied by the proposed amendment; claims filed by amendments should be substitute claims and must clearly state whether each claim is original, cancelled, replaced by proposed substitute, proposed substitute for X, or proposed new claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must clearly state where the specification and drawings support all limitations in proposed substitute claims; if the Board cannot determine support, the motion may be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of patentably distinct features
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to amend should clearly state the patentably distinct features for proposed substitute claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aids the Board in determining whether the amendment narrows the claims and whether the amendment is responsive to the grounds of unpatentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness limit on number of substitute claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of substitute claims must be 'reasonable.' There is a general presumption that one substitute claim would be needed to replace each challenged claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption may be rebutted by demonstrating need; the presumption balances the one-year timeline against the patent owner's need to define the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner opposition to motion to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners will have an opportunity to fully respond to a patent owner’s motion to amend and oppositions may include new evidence directed to proposed substitute claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No authorization needed to file an opposition; petitioners may submit new expert declarations responsive to the proposed substitute claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply limits (no new issues/evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply may only respond to arguments raised in the corresponding opposition; replies that raise new issues or belatedly present evidence will not be considered and may be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of new-issue indicators: new evidence necessary to make out a prima facie case for patentability/unpatentability or evidence that could have been presented in a prior filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other motions — scope and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may file many types of motions (e.g., to exclude evidence, to seal, for joinder, to file supplemental information, for judgment based on supplemental information, for observations on cross-examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relief sought is not identified in the rules, the party should arrange a conference call with the Board and opposing party to discuss; parties must comply with the appropriate rule requirements (e.g., §42.123/223 for supplemental information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information submission rules (§ 42.123/223)
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to submit supplemental information must meet timing and relevance requirements: (1) request authorization is made within one month of institution; (2) supplemental information must be relevant to a claim for which trial has been instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking to submit supplemental information more than one month after institution, the party must request authorization and show why the information could not reasonably have been obtained earlier and that consideration would be in the interests of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenging admissibility of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: To challenge admissibility, a party must object timely when evidence is offered and preserve the objection by filing a motion to exclude evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A motion to exclude must: (a) identify where in the record the objection originally was made; (b) identify where the evidence was relied upon by an opponent; (c) address objections to exhibits in numerical order; and (d) explain each objection. It should explain why the evidence is not admissible (e.g., relevance, hearsay) but may not be used to challenge sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observations on cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If cross-examination occurs after a party's last substantive paper on an issue, the party may file concise observations to call the Board’s attention to testimony that does not warrant a motion to exclude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations must be concise (one short paragraph), state the exhibit/page/lines and the testimony, identify relevance to a specific argument or exhibit, and not be used to raise new issues or re-argue. Opposing party may file an equally concise response. Observations without prior authorization may be prohibited; Board may refuse excessively long/argumentative observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument procedures and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party may present its case before at least three Board members; the time for requesting oral argument is set in the Scheduling Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical order: petitioner, patent owner/respondent, petitioner rebuttal (order can vary). Parties must notify special equipment/needs early. Demonstrative exhibits should be simple (handout/binder), pages numbered. Live testimony is generally unnecessary but may be allowed by motion. No new evidence or arguments may be presented at oral argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement encouragement and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board favors settlement and will facilitate settlement discussions; a proceeding will generally terminate after filing a settlement agreement unless the Board has already decided the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may require settlement discussion as part of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision timing and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: For IPR, PGR, and CBM the Board will enter a final written decision not more than one year from institution, extendable up to six months for good cause; the decision will address the issues necessary to resolve the proceeding. For derivation proceedings, the Board expects (though not statutorily) to provide a final decision within one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing request standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with a Board decision may file a request for rehearing; the burden is on the moving party to show the decision should be modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must specifically identify matters the party believes the Board misapprehended or overlooked and where each matter was previously addressed. Evidence not already of record will not be admitted absent good cause. Opposing parties should not file a response absent Board request. Requests are envisioned to be decided approximately one month after receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A — Due date structure for IPR/PGR/CBM
rubrics_metrics.description: A concrete schedule defines DUE DATES 1–7 mapping specific filings and relative timing (e.g., Due Date 1: patent owner response/motion to amend; Due Date 2: petitioner reply/opposition to motion to amend; Due Date 3: patent owner reply; Due Date 4: motions to exclude/request oral argument/motion for observation on cross; Due Date 5: patent owner response to observation/opposition to motion to exclude; Due Date 6: reply to opposition; Due Date 7: oral argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may stipulate different dates for Due Dates 1–5 (but not extend Due Dates 6–7). Typical target intervals shown (e.g., 3 months, 1 month, 3 weeks, 2 weeks, 1 week).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-examination begins after any supplemental evidence is due and ends no later than one week before the filing date for any paper in which the cross-examination testimony is expected to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may agree to different timing; scheduling considerations affect objections, supplementation, cross-examination, and drafting papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective Order purpose and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Protective orders govern treatment of confidential information in Board proceedings; parties are encouraged to agree to a stipulated protective order, otherwise a default standing protective order will be automatically entered. The terms take effect upon filing a Motion to Seal and remain until lifted or modified for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and marking of confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Producing parties must clearly mark documents or information considered confidential as 'PROTECTIVE ORDER MATERIAL'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When some information in a submission is confidential, parties should file redacted non-confidential versions and a confidential version under seal along with a Motion to Seal explaining why redacted portions are confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons entitled to access confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to confidential information is limited to defined categories: parties, representatives of record, retained experts who sign acknowledgements and certify non-competitor status, in-house counsel, other employees/consultants (only on agreement or Board order), Office employees (no acknowledgement required), and necessary support personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees/consultants (other than in-house counsel) require agreement of parties or Board order and opposing party bears burden to restrict access. Support personnel need not sign acknowledgements but must be informed of terms by those they assist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations to protect confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of confidential information must take reasonable care to maintain confidentiality, including secure storage, using efforts no less rigorous than for their own confidential information, ensuring support personnel understand obligations, and limiting copying to a reasonable number with recordkeeping of locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and redaction procedures for confidential submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing with the Board, a party may file documents under seal together with a non-confidential description of the nature of the sealed material and reasons for confidentiality; where only part is confidential, file a redacted non-confidential version and a confidential version under seal, plus a Motion to Seal setting out reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-confidential version must indicate redaction locations; confidential information stays under seal unless Board orders otherwise after motion/hearing or sua sponte.
